scenes.text: A robot on Mars once hummed Happy Birthday to itself, all alone.
NASA's Curiosity rover launched on November twenty sixth, twenty eleven.
It traveled about three hundred fifty million miles to get there.
Then a rocket powered sky crane lowered it on cables, about twenty five feet, into Gale Crater.
Curiosity weighs about two thousand pounds and runs on heat from plutonium, not solar panels.
But it has no speaker and no microphone.
So for its first anniversary on Mars, engineers used a lab inside it called SAM.
SAM normally vibrates to shake powdered rock into tiny sample cups.
By vibrating at just the right frequencies, it played the Happy Birthday tune.
Mars air is so thin that the song would have been very faint.
And it only happened once, in twenty thirteen.
Every command costs power and planning time, and music brings no scientific gain.
It was planned to work for one Martian year, but kept exploring for over a decade.
Should NASA let it sing again on its birthday? Tell me below.

title: The Mars rover that played Happy Birthday to itself 🎂
caption: NASA's Curiosity rover launched on Nov 26, 2011. For its first year on Mars, engineers made its SAM lab vibrate to the Happy Birthday tune, and it only did it once.
